sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Intermolecular Attraction**: Cohesion refers strictly to the attractive forces between **like molecules** due to electrostatic forces and quantum mechanical interactions.
• **Role in Surface Tension**: Molecules in the bulk liquid experience balanced forces in all directions, whereas surface molecules experience a net inward pull, generating **surface tension**.
• **Contrast with Adhesion**: Cohesion operates between identical molecules (e.g., water-to-water), whereas **adhesion** operates between different molecules (e.g., water-to-glass).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Magnitude depends heavily on molecular polarity and hydrogen bonding strength, making water exhibit exceptionally high cohesive force compared to organic solvents.

items.definition: The elastic tendency of a fluid surface acquired by the parallel cohesive forces acting on surface molecules, making it acquire the least possible surface area.
The ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces without the assistance of, or even in opposition to, external forces like gravity, driven by the interplay of cohesion and adhesion.
The mechanism of water movement upward through the xylem of plants, maintained by the high tensile strength resulting from continuous water-molecule cohesion.
The curve in the upper surface of a liquid close to the surface of the container, concave when adhesion exceeds cohesion (water-glass) and convex when cohesion exceeds adhesion (mercury-glass).

items.title: Major Biological & Geophysical Manifestations
items.content:
• **Xylem Transport in Tall Trees**: Cohesive forces allow water columns to withstand negative pressures (tensions) up to several megapascals without breaking.
• **Insect Locomotion**: Water striders walk on water surfaces relying entirely on the cohesive force-driven surface tension barrier.

items.title: Industrial & Technological Applications
items.content:
• **Detergents & Surfactants**: Added to water to artificially lower cohesive forces, allowing water to penetrate fabric pores effectively.
• **Welding & Soldering**: Relies on surface tension and wetting characteristics governed by relative cohesive and adhesive forces.

items.title: Mnemonic for Cohesion vs Adhesion
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'CO-hesion is CO-mpany (same), AD-hesion is AD-ding something different (different).'
• **Decoded Meaning**: Cohesion = same molecules; Adhesion = different molecules.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly prevents confusion in statements regarding meniscus and wetting action.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Contact angle < 90° means Adhesion > Cohesion (wets glass); Contact angle > 90° means Cohesion > Adhesion (does not wet glass).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that water rises in plants purely due to root pressure. Root pressure is insufficient for tall trees; the primary driver is the Cohesion-Tension theory powered by transpirational pull.

Mains Value Addition: When writing answers on plant physiology, drought-resistant crops, or biophysics, explicitly quote the 'Cohesion-Tension-Transpiration' pull model to showcase precise scientific depth.

keyTakeaways: Cohesive force is the intermolecular attraction between identical molecules, governing surface tension and droplet behavior.
The balance between cohesive and adhesive forces determines contact angles, meniscus shapes, and capillary rise.
In biological systems, water cohesion provides the extreme tensile strength required for water transport in tall trees against gravity.
